narrative:
The model estimates a 44% chance that you will leave your job. This probability is high enough for the organization to deny your promotion, as they prefer to invest in people more likely to stay long-term.

The decision was driven mainly by three aspects of your profile. First, your overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest factor. Most employees the model expects to stay have similar short experience, yet in your case this pushed the prediction toward leaving, suggesting the model sees early-career professionals in your situation as higher-risk. Second, the number of years you have spent in this current organization (also 1-5 years) worked in the opposite direction, pulling the prediction slightly toward staying because it matches the pattern of many stable employees. Third, not having received other job offers while working here also nudged the prediction toward staying, as the absence of external opportunities often signals loyalty.

Taken together, your relatively short total experience outweighed the stabilizing effects of your tenure here and lack of outside offers, tipping the balance toward expecting you to leave.

The organization should discuss with you how to strengthen your sense of belonging and growth within the medical sector. You may want to explore internal training opportunities or clearer promotion paths that could increase your commitment and reduce the risk of leaving. Addressing these points early could change both the model’s outlook and your actual decision to stay.
